comparison: Perfect agreement on ALG proliferation after injury (C19-C33). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED using multiple complementary techniques. OpenEval emphasizes methodological controls while peer reviewers highlight this as 'solid evidence' for glial plasticity.

Strong agreement on PCD regulation of ALG numbers (C36-C38). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on the >50% single-color MARCM clones and p35 effects, while peer reviewers acknowledge this as an 'elegant experimental combination' showing glial divisions refined by apoptosis. Note: Peer review R2 does not explicitly mention C39.

Strong agreement on EG-to-ALG transdifferentiation and Prospero requirement (C40-C52, C70). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from G-TRACE lineage tracing and functional knockdown, while peer reviewers explicitly note this 'interconversion of glial subtypes' as injury-independent and Prospero-dependent, identifying it as a study strength.

Perfect agreement on uncertainty regarding glia-to-neuron transdifferentiation (C53-C65, C71-C73). Both rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval questions whether cells are functional neurons or in transition due to lack of mature markers, while peer reviewers explicitly state 'Elav+ cells originating from glia do not express markers for mature neurons' and note that future studies are needed to determine if they will differentiate.

Agreement on background/clinical context claims (C1-C3, C74). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these are appropriately documented background claims, while peer reviewers accept them as established context without challenge. Peer R5 includes many additional background claims (C4-C18, C34-C35, C66-C69, C75-C77) that OpenEval addresses separately in R6 and R7.

Substantial overlap on conceptual framework and literature-based claims (C4-C18, C34, C66-C69, C75-C77). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval evaluates these as well-supported by citations establishing homology and conceptual framework, while peer reviewers group these with other background claims as accepted context for the study.

Partial overlap on summary claims (C12, C35). OpenEval R7 evaluates summary claims integrating major findings as SUPPORTED, while peer R5 includes these among broader background claims. OpenEval R7 also addresses C70-C73 which peer reviewers evaluate separately in R3 and R4.
